cards.title: The rate-distortion region for distributed lossy source coding
cards.formal: Determine R_p(D₁,D₂) for every pair of correlated finite-alphabet discrete memoryless sources, reconstruction alphabets and distortion functions in the model below. The requested form of a new characterization remains unspecified; the operational definition alone is not a new coding theorem.

cards.definitions: Fix nonempty finite sets X₁,X₂,Ŷ₁,Ŷ₂, a probability mass function p on X₁×X₂, functions d_i:X_i×Ŷ_i→[0,∞) with finite values, and thresholds D_i≥0. The pairs (X₁,t,X₂,t), t=1,…,n, are independent with common law p. A length-n code consists of positive integers M₁,M₂, functions f_i:X_i^n→{1,…,M_i}, and a joint decoder g:{1,…,M₁}×{1,…,M₂}→Ŷ₁^n×Ŷ₂^n. Write (Ŷ₁^n,Ŷ₂^n)=g(f₁(X₁^n),f₂(X₂^n)). Encoder i sees only its own source block; descriptions reach the decoder without transmission errors. Codes are deterministic, agreed in advance, and there is no interaction or decoder side information. For ε>0 a code meets rates R_i and distortions D_i within ε when (log₂ M_i)/n≤R_i+ε and E[(1/n)∑ₜ d_i(X_i,t,Ŷ_i,t)]≤D_i+ε for both i. R_p(D₁,D₂) consists of nonnegative pairs (R₁,R₂) for which such codes exist for every ε>0 at all sufficiently large n. This includes limiting boundary rates. Expectation is over the source pairs. Computation and codebook size are unrestricted; rates count bits per source symbol.
cards.answer_criterion: A characterization must prove both achievability of every stated rate pair and impossibility outside its region for every model instance. Before this becomes a complete benchmark, the source must also specify the required mathematical representation or effective approximation guarantee. Repeating the operational definition does not settle that missing requirement.

context_blocks.title: Correlated observations, separate descriptions
context_blocks.text: Two sensors can observe related data without seeing each other’s recordings. Their common decoder can exploit correlation, while each sensor must choose its description from its own recording. For identical fair binary sources and zero Hamming distortion, sending the first recording at one bit per sample and sending nothing from the second sensor suffices. For independent fair bits, those same rates cannot reconstruct the second recording. Hamming distortion counts the fraction of incorrectly reconstructed symbols.

context_blocks.title: What the tradeoff measures
context_blocks.text: Higher distortion permits less accurate reconstructions and potentially lower rates. The target is the entire set of feasible pairs of description rates for fixed tolerances. It neither requires exact recovery of every block nor merely asks for the smallest sum of the two rates. A useful exact theorem must match an achievable region with a converse excluding every other pair.

context_blocks.title: Known results have specific scope
context_blocks.text: Slepian–Wolf resolves lossless reconstruction. Courtade and Weissman give an exact region for logarithmic loss, where a reconstruction is a probability distribution and the penalty is minus the logarithm of the probability assigned to the actual symbol. That setting does not settle arbitrary distortion tables on the finite reconstruction alphabets specified here. The general Berger–Tung achievable bound is not by itself a general converse.

context_blocks.title: Status and remaining formulation issue
context_blocks.text: Malak’s January 2025 manuscript explicitly lists general lossy multiterminal coding as unresolved. Its May 2026 revision studies distributed computation of matrix and dot products, a different reconstruction task. The inherited question also leaves an editorial gap: “characterize” does not say which finite expression or effective guarantee a new answer must supply. The present card defines the coding model while retaining that gap.

cards.context:
Two sensors can observe related data without seeing each other’s recordings. Their common decoder can exploit correlation, while each sensor must choose its description from its own recording. For identical fair binary sources and zero Hamming distortion, sending the first recording at one bit per sample and sending nothing from the second sensor suffices. For independent fair bits, those same rates cannot reconstruct the second recording. Hamming distortion counts the fraction of incorrectly reconstructed symbols.

Higher distortion permits less accurate reconstructions and potentially lower rates. The target is the entire set of feasible pairs of description rates for fixed tolerances. It neither requires exact recovery of every block nor merely asks for the smallest sum of the two rates. A useful exact theorem must match an achievable region with a converse excluding every other pair.

Slepian–Wolf resolves lossless reconstruction. Courtade and Weissman give an exact region for logarithmic loss, where a reconstruction is a probability distribution and the penalty is minus the logarithm of the probability assigned to the actual symbol. That setting does not settle arbitrary distortion tables on the finite reconstruction alphabets specified here. The general Berger–Tung achievable bound is not by itself a general converse.

Malak’s January 2025 manuscript explicitly lists general lossy multiterminal coding as unresolved. Its May 2026 revision studies distributed computation of matrix and dot products, a different reconstruction task. The inherited question also leaves an editorial gap: “characterize” does not say which finite expression or effective guarantee a new answer must supply. The present card defines the coding model while retaining that gap.

meta.status_scope: No claim of exhaustive open-status verification
methodology: Detailed cards have individually written statements, context, significance, and documented results. Source notes are unfinished research records and do not yet meet that standard. The legacy index is retained for traceability.
Open in the source means open at the date of that source. The build date, 10 September 2026, does not establish current open status. Old excerpts may omit conditions or subsequent results.

Selection considers model power, necessary resources, sharp bounds, structural characterizations, explicit constructions, and minimal assumptions. Source notes use a heuristic screen; detailed cards give an individual explanation.

The earlier automatic paper screen allowed at most one new card per paper title and rejected identical formulations and close duplicates within a source. Approved textbook and survey imports retain multiple distinct questions per publication. Confirmed overlaps supplement existing cards; collection-wide semantic deduplication remains incomplete.

Short quotations retain the source language. Later related literature, where listed, is a research aid rather than evidence of resolution. Personal notes and saved cards are stored locally in your browser.

Textbook and survey questions are dated paraphrases; source locations, conjectures, research directions and caveats are preserved on the problem cards. These annotations do not establish current open status or change a later card review. New source drafts remain unassessed for importance. The reader contains the imported questions and external bibliographic references only; source files are not bundled.

Selection groups follow the agreed 10 large and 25 small categories. We aim for benchmarks of 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. All three use the same category order and the same ranking within each category. The respective prefixes are 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 problems per large/small category. The possible 1,000-problem expansion has 1000 assigned places and 0 reserved places. Each card records its category explicitly. These counts describe saved candidates; classification does not verify a statement or its current open status. Deleted records are absent from the catalogue and exports. Their stable IDs and reasons are retained to prevent reimport. Final quota selection and a comprehensive deduplication audit remain pending.

Importance ordering is an editorial assessment of foundational significance, breadth of consequences, and influence on other questions. Each assessed card gives a reason. The category-wide review also uses shared priority bands for questions of comparable scope; it does not claim that these ties have a scientifically meaningful internal order. Unassessed drafts share a provisional score of 50; their relative order is only an ID tie-break, not an importance judgment. The first 5/2 places in each large/small category are an explicit editorial focus selection balancing importance and topical diversity. Focus ordering does not alter importance scores; remaining candidates use score and ID order. The targets are 100 and 500 problems, with a possible expansion to 1,000. Top 100, Top 500 and the possible Top 1000 use the first 5/2, 25/10 and 50/20 category places respectively, all from the same ranking. Category positions include all candidates and remain fixed when filtering. Publication date, source date, and card detail do not increase importance. Records marked resolved are placed after the remaining candidates, without changing their historical importance score. Importance review does not establish that a saved question is still open.

benchmark_selection.basis: Individual editorial review of saved titles, importance rationales, problem statements, source notes and working summaries. This is a review of importance and topical diversity, not a fresh verification of open status or completion of draft formulations. Importance scores are preserved.
